lessonsIntro: We couldn't find a surf school teaching at Kimmeridge. It's a rocky reef break, so it's best for surfers who already have some experience.

text: Kimmeridge Bay is known as one of the best reef breaks on the south coast, with rock ledges rather than sand. Windsurf guide boards.co.uk says the waves are often bigger than at Bournemouth, there's little shorebreak, and the reef is best from mid to high tide on the push. It suits intermediate and better water users; the Ledges are the friendliest part and Broad Bench is for experts only.

It isn't a place to learn. The ledges are rocky and very slippery, especially from mid to low tide, so you need to walk in and out carefully. The bay is surrounded by cliffs, with limited access at high tide, and the nearby army firing range means you should keep out of the area when the red flags are flying. We found no lifeguard cover here.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Intermediate and up
cards.text: A reef break over slippery rock ledges. Learn on a sandy beach first.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Mid to high tide, rising
cards.text: The reef works best on the push, with a south-west swell and the wind swinging west or north-west.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Rocks and firing range
cards.text: Shallow, slippery ledges and the range's red flags. The bay is backed by cliffs.

hireIntro: We couldn't confirm any surf hire at or near Kimmeridge, so bring your own kit.

text: Kimmeridge's reef waves have more push than most of this coast, so improvers usually bring a hard board they're comfortable on, such as a mid-length or shortboard. Reef boots are worth wearing for the slippery rock ledges. There's no hire or shop at the bay, so come with everything you need, including a spare leash.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Your own hard board
cards.text: A mid-length or shortboard for reef waves. Not a beginner spot.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: Season-dependent
cards.text: We couldn't confirm a sea-temperature source for this stretch of coast. As a general rule on the English Channel, most people wear a 4/3mm in late spring and autumn and a 5/4mm with boots in winter; check with the school or shop before you go.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Windsurf and wing
cards.text: boards.co.uk covers it as a windsurf spot too. Keep clear of the firing range when red flags are up.

shopsIntro: There's no surf shop at Kimmeridge; the nearest we could confirm is in Boscombe, Bournemouth.
shopsText: Kimmeridge is a small village with no surf shop or kit hire at the bay. The nearest surf shop we could confirm is Down The Line Surf on Sea Road in Boscombe, Bournemouth, which stocks surfboards. Poole has watersports shops too, but we couldn't confirm which ones are still trading, so check before you travel.

lessons.a: It isn't a beginner spot. It's a reef break over slippery rock ledges, better for intermediate surfers.

lessons.q: Are there surf lessons at Kimmeridge?
lessons.a: We couldn't find any school teaching here.
boards.co.uk says mid to high tide on the push, with care needed over the rocks at lower tides.

hire.q: Can I hire a board at Kimmeridge?
hire.a: We couldn't find any hire at the bay, so bring your own kit.
It's a good idea. The rock ledges are very slippery underfoot.

shops.a: The nearest we could confirm is Down The Line Surf in Boscombe, Bournemouth.
